newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay commuters head home to escape cyclone fury.
newsitem.headline: Bombay commuters head home to escape cyclone fury.

text.p: Hundreds of commuters in India's commercial capital made their way home on Thursday as civic authorities prepared to batten down the hatches ahead of cyclonic storms expected to later lash the city.
Winds ranging from 80 kmph to 90 kmph, accompanied by heavy rainfall, will hit the city late on Thursday as a cyclone passes near by, weather bureau officials said.
"Bombay will not be in the eye of the cyclone, but places near Bombay will probably be in the eye of the storm," state-run television said in a broadcast shortly after noon.

State government officials said they had advised all schools and colleges to close from 2 p.m. (0830 GMT). Civic authorities said they had shut down the Bombay Municipal Corporation's network of 1,600 public schools.
Private schools and some offices had also shut down for the day, they added.
The cyclone, now about 250 km off the coast of Bombay in a west-southwest direction, is expected to hit the neighbouring state of Gujarat late tonight, the weather bureau said.
Fishermen have been warned not to venture out to sea for the next 24 hours.
"Fishermen have been warned not to go to sea, and danger signals have been hoisted in the ports," a weather bureau official said.
North Maharashtra and south Gujarat will be the worst affected by the cyclone.
"The cyclone is travelling in a northerly direction and is expected to hit the coast between Dahanu and Veraval in the night," a weather bureau official told Reuters.
Dahanu is about 100 km north of Bombay while Veraval is a small fishing port on the south Gujarat coast, about 332 km northwest of Bombay.

"Rain or thundershowers are likely at almost all the places with heavy to very heavy falls at a few places in the coastal districts of Gujarat state and one or two places in Konkan and Goa during the next 24 hours," a statement by the India Meteorological Department said.
